Since OAuth refresh responses (e.g., Microsoft) can omit refresh_token, this overwrites the real refresh token with junk, breaking re-authentication. The mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal junk string "refresh_token" into `data.refresh_token` whenever the parsed response lacks a refresh_token, and callers persist that parsed data directly into `credential.key`. Office365CalendarService spreads the parsed data over the existing credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...data}` at lines 259-260) and writes via `prisma.credential.update`, overwriting the only stored copy of the user's real OAuth refresh token with the placeholder; this fires on every refresh in sharing mode (the minimum schema strips the real token before the check) and in default mode whenever a provider legitimately omits refresh_token from a refresh response (Microsoft does for some tenants) — where the old spread-only-present-fields code preserved it — leaving the integration unrecoverable without user re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed refresh response lacks a `refresh_token` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In `Office365CalendarService`, the new code calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`) before persisting via `prisma.credential.update` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on parse failure, `tokenResponse.success` will be true, so the injected placeholder refresh_token will overwrite the previously stored real refresh token whenever the provider omits `refresh_token` in the refresh response (and in sharing-mode parsing via `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which doesn't require/ensure a real refresh_token). This is a verifiable data-loss/irrecoverable-auth bug introduced by the diff.
